title: Sequence collapse and token harmonization for charts & tables
creator: Sofia Ramos
description: Consolidate redundant state sequences across chart and table components and align semantic tokens used by those components. The goal is to collapse long state variant chains (hover -> hover-alt -> hover-strong) into a predictable state stack, normalize spacing tokens applied by auto-layout frames, and introduce a clear naming scheme for the revised components so they publish cleanly without breaking consumer instances. This includes a small migration plan for teams consuming charts/tables in product repositories and a publish gating checklist to avoid regressions.
acceptance_criteria: All chart and table components reduced to a maximum of 4 visual states per component (default, hover, active/focus, disabled) and documented in the token matrix.
Semantic tokens used by charts/tables (color, border, elevation, spacing) mapped to existing global tokens with no ad-hoc local tokens remaining.
Auto-layout frames for table rows and chart legend blocks have stable axis constraints (no nested percent constraints) and pass the publish CI checks.
Renaming scheme applied: <component>-<role>-<size> (e.g., table-row-primary-sm) and a migration guide published with automated Figma detach/replace suggestions.
Design QA checklist completed and sign-off from PM and Eng reviewers; no critical regressions reported in the smoke tests for modules depending on the library.
